title: NY State Senate · District 32
area: South and central Bronx, including parts of Parkchester, Soundview, West Farms, Hunts Point, Longwood, Concourse, Melrose, Morrisania, Mott Haven, East Tremont, and Westchester Square.

context.text: The Democratic primary scheduled for June 23, 2026 was canceled and incumbent Luis Sepúlveda advanced without appearing on the ballot; the Republican primary was also canceled. As of this writing, no Republican or other opposition candidate has filed for the general election, leaving Sepúlveda unopposed on the ballot.

candidates.name: Luis Sepúlveda
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed; no Republican or third-party opponent has filed for the general election.
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 32 (since April 2018)

summary.text: Luis Sepúlveda is the Democratic nominee for re-election to New York State Senate District 32 in the central Bronx. An attorney, he served three terms in the State Assembly before winning an April 2018 special election to the Senate, where he chairs the Judiciary and Cities 1 committees. He is unopposed in the general election.

background.text: Born in Brooklyn on February 11, 1964, according to Wikipedia.

Earned a bachelor's degree and a J.D. (1991) from Hofstra University and its Maurice A. Deane School of Law; his official biography describes him as one of two Latinx attorneys in the New York State Legislature.
Worked as an attorney at Community Law Practice and as an adjunct professor at Mercy College.
Lost the 2010 Democratic primary for the 87th Assembly District to incumbent Peter M. Rivera, then won the seat in 2012 after Rivera retired.

Served three terms as Assemblymember for the 87th Assembly District (2013–2018), including on the Aging, Agriculture, Banks, Correction, Housing, and Mental Hygiene committees, before his April 2018 election to the State Senate.
Won the April 2018 special election to the 32nd Senate District, succeeding Rubén Díaz Sr., who left to join the New York City Council.

As a State Senator, helped lead the 2019 criminal-justice reforms ending cash bail for most misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies and establishing new discovery and speedy-trial rules; lead sponsor of the Jose Peralta DREAM Act and the Green Light Law.

On January 12, 2021, was arrested on a charge of criminal obstruction of breathing after his wife alleged he had choked her during a domestic dispute; he and his wife each accused the other of assault, and his lawyer called her claim false. Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins removed him as chair of the Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee and stripped his other committee assignments. The Bronx District Attorney's office dropped all charges on October 4, 2021, stating it could not meet the burden of proof and that his wife did not wish to testify against him.

Chairs the Senate Judiciary Committee (a role Wikipedia dates to January 2026) and the Select Majority Task Force on Diversity in the Judiciary; according to his official biography, in 2022 he became the first New York State Senator granted Dominican citizenship.

priorities.text: Criminal justice reform, including ending cash bail and expanding pretrial discovery and speedy-trial protections.
Immigrant rights, including as a sponsor of the Jose Peralta New York State DREAM Act and the Green Light Law extending driver's licenses to undocumented New Yorkers.
Mental health services, including suicide-prevention programs for Latina teenagers.
Funding for universal pre-kindergarten in New York City.

positions.summary: Sponsored the Jose Peralta New York State DREAM Act, giving undocumented students access to state financial aid, and the Green Light Law, which extends driver's licenses to undocumented New Yorkers regardless of immigration status.

record.text: Sponsored S10604, expanding the Judicial Security Act to cover judges' domestic partners and children of any age and streamlining procedures to keep judges' personal information confidential; passed the Senate 60-1 on June 2, 2026 and was substituted by, and returned to the Assembly as, A11388.

Sponsored S10591, authorizing the Court of Appeals to permit electronic filing and service of civil briefs, motions, and criminal leave applications; passed the Senate 61-0 on June 2, 2026 and was substituted by, and returned to the Assembly as, A11389.
Sponsored S10483, exempting student legislative interns from the state's two-year post-employment lobbying ban; in Senate Ethics and Internal Governance Committee as of May 15, 2026.

Was arrested January 12, 2021 on a charge of criminal obstruction of breathing following a domestic dispute with his wife, in which each accused the other of assault; removed as chair of the Crime Victims, Crime and Correction Committee and stripped of other committee assignments by Senate leadership. The Bronx District Attorney's office dropped all charges October 4, 2021, stating it could not meet the burden of proof and that his wife did not wish to testify against him.
Chairs the Senate Judiciary Committee and the Select Majority Task Force on Diversity in the Judiciary in the 2025–2026 session, and also chairs the Cities 1 Committee.
